answer.answer: To update your Social Security card after a legal name change due to marriage, you need to tell Social Security so you can get a corrected card, and if you are working, also tell your employer. The evidence of the legal name change can include a marriage document, divorce decree, certificate of naturalization showing the new name, or a court order approving the name change. Documents must be current and not expired; photocopies, notarized copies, and receipts showing you applied for a document are not accepted. If the name-change document does not give enough information to identify you in SSA records, or if you changed your name more than two years ago, you must show an identity document in your prior name as shown in SSA records (an expired identity document in your old name is acceptable); if you lack one, SSA may accept an unexpired identity document in your new name if your identity can be properly established. For your New York driver's license, bring to a DMV office a completed Application for Permit, Driver License or Non-Driver ID Card (MV-44), your current license (or at least 6 points of proof of identity), and the original or certified copy of your U.S. marriage certificate (or U.S. divorce documents or other court papers for a name change issued in the U.S.). You must also update your photo when you change your name on your license. In addition, if the name on your license application does not match the name on your identity, lawful status, and Social Security proofs, you must bring court or government-issued proof documenting the event causing the name change, such as a marriage license, divorce decree, adoption, or court order document. The DMV process also requires a new photo.

For your Social Security card: because you legally changed your name due to marriage, you need to tell Social Security so you can get a corrected card; if you are working, also tell your employer. If you lack an identity document in your prior name, SSA may accept an unexpired identity document in your new name if your identity can be properly established. SSA cannot accept photocopies or notarized copies, or a receipt showing you applied for a document, and all documents must be current and not expired. One document may serve two purposes (for example, a U.S. passport as proof of both citizenship and identity).

response.answer: To apply for GI Bill education benefits, first check whether you're eligible for VA education benefits, gather the documents and information you'll need, and see what benefits you'll get at the school you want to attend using the GI Bill Comparison Tool. The documents and information needed to apply include your Social Security number, bank account direct deposit information, your education and military history, and basic information about the school or training facility you want to attend or are attending now. You can submit your Application for VA Benefits (VA Form 22-1990) online, or apply by mail, in person, or with the help of a trained professional. By mail, call 888-GI-BILL-1 (888-442-4551), Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. ET, to request that the application be sent to you, then fill it out and mail it to the VA regional claims processing office in the same location as your school. In person, go to a VA regional benefit office and have a VA employee help you. After applying, ask your school or training program to certify your enrollment; the certifying official may be in your school's financial aid, Veterans affairs, registrar, admissions, or counseling office. Note that if you're applying for Vocational Rehabilitation and Employment (Chapter 31) or educational and career counseling (Chapter 36) benefits, you'll need to use a different application. answer.answer: To get another copy of your lost DD214, you can request it by submitting a Standard Form 180, Request Pertaining to Military Records, from the National Archives; you can request military service records online, by mail, or by fax. To add veteran status to your New York driver's license, as a qualified U.S. military veteran who was honorably discharged with a NY State driver license, you can have the word "Veteran" printed on the upper left hand of your photo document. There is no additional fee for the veteran status designation, but all regular transaction fees will apply. To apply, you must provide proof of an honorable discharge, such as a U.S. Department of Defense Form DD-214 that indicates an honorable discharge. You can apply by mail by sending a completed Application for Permit, Driver License or Non-Driver ID Card (MV-44), your proof of honorable discharge (send photocopies, not original documents), to DMV License Production Bureau, Room 331, 6 Empire State Plaza, Albany, NY 12228. You cannot apply by phone or online. If you have a Standard license and want to change to a REAL ID or Enhanced while adding veteran status, you must come into a DMV office and bring your proof of honorable discharge (original or photocopies).

answer.answer: You can get a replacement DD214 by submitting a Standard Form 180 (Request Pertaining to Military Records) to the National Archives; requests can be made online, by mail, or by fax (E3). Separately, because you were honorably discharged and hold a NY State driver license, you may have the word "Veteran" printed on your photo document at no additional fee, though regular transaction fees apply (E2, E4). To apply you must provide proof of honorable discharge—for example, a DD-214 indicating an honorable discharge (E2). You can apply by mail by sending a completed MV-44 application, photocopies of your proof of honorable discharge, and your original documents to the DMV License Production Bureau, Room 331, 6 Empire State Plaza, Albany, NY 12228; you cannot apply by phone or online (E6). If you also want to change to a REAL ID or Enhanced document while adding veteran status, you must apply in person at a DMV office and bring your proof of honorable discharge (original or photocopies) (E6). Once the veteran designation is added, it will automatically appear on future DMV documents when you replace or renew (E2).

VA disability compensation: This is a monthly tax-free payment to Veterans who got sick or injured while serving in the military, or whose service made an existing condition worse; you may qualify for physical conditions such as a chronic illness or injury. Eligibility generally requires that you served on active duty, active duty for training, or inactive duty training, and that you have a disability rating for your service-connected condition, plus at least one additional listed requirement (for example, an in-service disability claim linking the condition to illness or injury during service). A leg injury incurred during military service that causes major difficulty walking could potentially support a claim, subject to meeting these criteria.

New York disabled parking permit: New York requires proof of disability when applying for a parking permit or plates. If you have an obvious, visible, permanent disability—such as complete or partial loss of a leg or foot—the medical statement requirement may be waived by the local issuing agent for a permit (or by a DMV supervisor for plates). If you moved to New York, you must still provide the required proof of disability even if you had parking privileges elsewhere, and an out-of-state permit cannot be exchanged for a NYS permit or plates.

answer.answer: For the DMV part: New York issues disabled parking permits (and license plates) to people with qualifying disabilities. A qualifying disability includes one that constitutes an equal degree of disability, imposes unusual hardship in the use of public transportation, and prevents the person from getting around without great difficulty. A temporary permit valid for six months may be issued when a person has a temporarily disabling condition that makes the person unable to walk without a cane, crutches, a walker, or other assisting device. To qualify, you must present proof of the disability from an acceptable medical professional — a medical doctor (MD), doctor of osteopathy (DO), or doctor of podiatric medicine (DPM) licensed in NYS only, or an optometrist (OD) for blindness. If you have an obvious, visible, permanent disability such as complete or partial loss of a leg or foot, the medical statement requirement may be waived by a DMV supervisor for license plates or by the local issuing agent for a permit. If you moved to NYS, you must provide the required proof of disability even if you had parking privileges elsewhere, and an out-of-state permit cannot be exchanged for a NYS permit or plates. Check with your local issuing agent before applying.

How does a veteran apply for VA disability compensation?
What are the requirements to obtain a disabled parking permit in New York?

response.answer: For the DMV part: New York issues disabled parking permits (and license plates) to people with qualifying disabilities. A qualifying disability includes one that constitutes an equal degree of disability, imposes unusual hardship in the use of public transportation, and prevents the person from getting around without great difficulty. A temporary permit valid for six months may be issued when a person has a temporarily disabling condition that makes the person unable to walk without a cane, crutches, a walker, or other assisting device. To qualify, you must present proof of the disability from an acceptable medical professional — a medical doctor (MD), doctor of osteopathy (DO), or doctor of podiatric medicine (DPM) licensed in NYS only, or an optometrist (OD) for blindness. If you have an obvious, visible, permanent disability such as complete or partial loss of a leg or foot, the medical statement requirement may be waived by a DMV supervisor for license plates or by the local issuing agent for a permit. If you moved to NYS, you must provide the required proof of disability even if you had parking privileges elsewhere, and an out-of-state permit cannot be exchanged for a NYS permit or plates. Check with your local issuing agent before applying.

answer.answer:
You may be able to seek both VA disability compensation and a New York disabled parking permit, but they are separate processes with different requirements.

VA disability compensation: VA disability compensation is a monthly tax-free payment to Veterans who got sick or injured while serving in the military, or whose service made an existing condition worse. You may qualify for benefits for physical conditions such as a chronic illness or injury. Generally, you must have a current illness or injury (a condition affecting your body or mind) and meet at least one listed requirement; both of these must be true: you served on active duty, active duty for training, or inactive duty training, and you have a disability rating for your service-connected condition. The evidence does not specify how to apply or how a rating is determined.

New York disabled parking permit: New York issues permits (and plates) to people with qualifying disabilities. A qualifying disability includes one that constitutes an equal degree of disability, imposes unusual hardship in the use of public transportation, and prevents the person from getting around without great difficulty. A temporary permit valid for six months may be issued for a temporarily disabling condition that makes the person unable to walk without a cane, crutches, a walker, or other assisting device. To qualify, you must present proof of the disability from an acceptable medical professional: a medical doctor (MD), doctor of osteopathy (DO), or doctor of podiatric medicine (DPM) licensed in NYS only, or an optometrist (OD) for blindness. If you have an obvious, visible, permanent disability such as complete or partial loss of a leg or foot, the medical statement requirement may be waived by a DMV supervisor for license plates or by the local issuing agent for a permit. If you moved to NYS, you must provide the required proof of disability even if you had parking privileges elsewhere, and an out-of-state permit cannot be exchanged for a NYS permit or plates. Check with your local issuing agent before applying.

These are independent programs; the evidence does not establish that a VA rating qualifies you for a NY permit or vice versa.

answer.answer: To arrange burial in a VA national cemetery, you may want to choose a funeral director to help plan the burial, then either you or the funeral director must take steps to schedule the burial, including gathering the information and documents needed to identify the deceased when calling the National Cemetery Scheduling Office. You'll need the DD214 or other discharge documents of the Veteran whose military service will be used to determine eligibility for burial in a VA national cemetery; the discharge must have been under conditions other than dishonorable. Other documents may also be needed to verify relationship or dependent status, such as a death certificate. If you can't find these documents, ask for help when you call. For the New York driver's license, mail a copy of the death certificate and a photocopy of his license or ID (if you have it) to the DMV License Production Bureau, P.O. Box 2688 ESP, Albany, NY 12220-0668, to prevent further mailings or identity theft. For registration, it may be possible to request a refund of the deceased individual's registration fee, which DMV will issue in the name of the estate. For transferring vehicle ownership when the owner is deceased, a checklist (MV-843) is available; under New York's Estates, Powers & Trust Law, the owner of one vehicle valued at $25,000 or less automatically transfers to the surviving spouse, who must print the decedent's name in the Seller's Name Print in Full section.

Income - driven repayment IDR plans are designed to make your student loan debt more manageable by reducing your monthly payment amount. response.answer: To get an official letter showing your Social Security benefits, log in to your my Social Security account for instant access to your benefit verification letter. If you already have an account, sign in, go to Replacement Documents on the right side of the screen, and choose get a Benefit Verification Letter to view, save, and print your personalized letter. If you don't have an account, you can create a free my Social Security account in less than 10 minutes, which lets you download or print your benefit verification letter. The benefit verification letter serves as proof of your retirement benefits and may be used as proof for loans and other income verification purposes; it includes your name, date of birth, and the benefit you receive. For income-driven repayment (IDR), these plans are designed to make student loan debt more manageable by reducing your monthly payment amount. The IDR request is for borrowers not currently on an IDR plan who want a lower monthly payment on their federal student loans, and for borrowers already on an IDR plan who need to recertify or make changes. When you apply, you'll be asked to provide income information used to determine eligibility for the PAYE or IBR plans and to calculate your monthly payment under all IDR plans; this may be your adjusted gross income (AGI) or alternative documentation of income. Your AGI is used if you filed a federal income tax return in the past two years and your current income isn't significantly different from the income on your most recent return. If you currently receive taxable income, you must submit a paper Income-Driven Repayment Plan Request with alternative documentation of your income, such as a pay stub. If you have more than one servicer for the loans you want to repay under an IDR plan, you must submit a separate request to each servicer.

For the FAFSA side: the provided evidence does not describe any FAFSA updates needed when transferring schools, so that part of your question cannot be answered from the available evidence.

evidence.text:
Eligibility for Veterans Pension 
The Veterans Pension program provides monthly payments to wartime Veterans who meet certain age or disability requirements, and who have income and net worth within certain limits. Find out if you re eligible for this benefit. 

Am I eligible for Veterans Pension benefits from VA? 
If you meet the VA pension eligibility requirements listed below , you may be eligible for the Veterans Pension program. Both of these must be true : You didn t receive a dishonorable discharge , and Your yearly family income and net worth meet certain limits set by Congress. Your net worth includes all personal property you own except your house, your car, and most home furnishings, minus any debt you owe. Your net worth includes the net worth of your spouse. answer.answer: For a VA Veterans Pension, eligibility depends on several factors: you must have served on active duty for at least 24 months and meet at least one of these conditions—being at least 65 years old, having a permanent and total disability, being a patient in a nursing home for long-term care because of a disability, or getting Social Security Disability Insurance or Supplemental Security Income. You must also have served during an eligible wartime period (such as the Mexican Border period, World War I, World War II, the Korean conflict, or the Vietnam War era), must not have received a dishonorable discharge, and your yearly family income and net worth must meet limits set by Congress (net worth includes your spouse's net worth and all personal property except your house, car, and most home furnishings, minus debts). For Social Security retirement benefits, you can start your retirement benefit at any point from age 62 up until age 70, with the amount higher the longer you delay; applying before full retirement age reduces your benefit, while delaying past full retirement age up to age 70 increases it through Delayed Retirement Credits. If you are within three months of age 65 or older and not ready to start monthly Social Security benefits, you can use the online retirement application to sign up just for Medicare and apply for retirement benefits later.

You must also have served during an eligible wartime period recognized under current law.

answer.answer: VA Veterans Pension: Based on the VA evidence, you may qualify if both of these are true: you didn't receive a dishonorable discharge, and your yearly family income and net worth meet limits set by Congress (net worth includes all personal property you own except your house, your car, and most home furnishings, minus any debt you owe, and includes your spouse's net worth). You must also have served on active duty for at least 24 months and meet at least one of these: you are at least 65 years old, have a permanent and total disability, are a patient in a nursing home for long-term care because of a disability, or are getting Social Security Disability Insurance or Supplemental Security Income. You must also have served during an eligible wartime period recognized under current law. Social Security retirement benefits: The evidence indicates you can start your retirement benefit at any point from age 62 up until age 70, with the amount higher the longer you delay starting; applying before full retirement age reduces your benefit (for example, with a full retirement age of 66, starting at 65 gives 93.33 percent of your full benefit amount), and delaying past full retirement age up to age 70 can increase it through Delayed Retirement Credits. The evidence also notes that if you are within three months of age 65 or older and not ready to start monthly Social Security benefits, you can use the online retirement application to sign up just for Medicare and wait to apply for retirement benefits later. answer.answer: To move your VA disability compensation direct deposit to your new account, update your direct deposit information in your VA.gov profile if the direct deposit feature appears there; if it doesn't appear, sign in to eBenefits to change it. You'll need your bank's routing number and account number. You can also change VA direct deposit information by mail using VA Form 24-0296 or by phone at 800-827-1000. To move your Social Security retirement direct deposit, log in to your my Social Security account, select the blue Benefits & Payment Details link, select Update Direct Deposit, choose whether you are the owner or co-owner of the account, enter your bank account information, review and verify it, then select Submit and Done. response.answer: To replace a lost New York driver's license, you can replace a license that was lost, stolen, or destroyed. If you already have an Enhanced or REAL ID, or you want to keep your Standard, you can replace by mail, and your document type will stay the same. For a mail replacement, send a completed Application for Permit, Driver License or Non-Driver ID Card (MV-44) — if you do not know your DMV ID number, enter your date of birth and name as it appeared on your old document — along with photocopies of acceptable proof of identity and payment of $17.50 by check or money order payable to "Commissioner of Motor Vehicles" to NYS Department of Motor Vehicles, 207 Genesee Street, Suite 6U, Utica, NY 13501-2874. The fee is $17.50; if you apply by mail or at a DMV office you can pay by credit/debit card or a check or money order made out to Commissioner of Motor Vehicles, while to apply online you must use a credit/debit card. The evidence does not state what license information the FAFSA asks for.

Note that interest accrues during forbearance and, if unpaid, will capitalize (be added to your principal balance).
